An Adventure in Space and Time was, for my money, one of the best things to come out of the anniversary year. I have at times been inclined to call it the best thing to have gone out under the Doctor Who name ever, but that's probably debatable.

Anyway! If you were to make (or pitch to Gatiss or suchlike) further films, which eras of Doctor Who would you go for? Perhaps more importantly, which eras have a story to tell? Whilst I can imagine Gareth Roberts could write a brilliant Graham Williams era movie, and there's probably something fantastic to be done with the wilderness years, there are only two stories that immediately jump out at me personally:

One about JNT. His time on Doctor Who was a long one, certainly, and also a turbulent one. Whilst it’s not always regarded to be a highlight, I think it’s fair to say that he made a huge contribution to the show. A documentary focusing on his time as producer would have definitely been a great celebration of a large part of Doctor Who’s history. The other obvious one would be RTD and the revival, because that’s really one of the trinity of big events across the last 50 years - the birth of Doctor Who, the death of Doctor Who, and the rebirth of Doctor Who.

They seem to present stories, I think, in the same way that An Adventure in Space and Time did; the first followed the story of Hartnell, and these films could/would follow the stories of JNT, or RTD. (Or, say, Julie Gardner or something)

Any thoughts? Casting ideas, maybe, or suggestions for a different era? The Moffat Movie? The handover from Derrick Sherwin to Barry Letts?
